rationale: Taking significant profits on META. Position was 96% of portfolio — an existential concentration risk. META thesis remains intact (Muse AI agent, 3.4M downloads, subscription monetization, zero sell ratings, Cantor target $860), but a single-stock bet of this magnitude is imprudent risk management regardless of conviction. At 261% unrealized gain from $198.53 avg, booking some is correct. Trimming ~38% of shares reduces from 620 to ~385 shares, keeping META as a dominant position while freeing capital for diversification and macro hedges. Exit condition for remaining: thesis breaks if Muse monetization disappoints in Q3 earnings, or if Fed hikes above 5% and multiple compression overrides earnings growth.

Macro hedge via ProShares UltraShort 20+ Year Treasury. The Fed under Warsh hiked 25bp in September and 16/18 officials see another hike in 2026. 10Y UST at 5.22%, 30Y at 5.53% — highest since 2004/2007 respectively. BNP Paribas projects 30Y hitting 5.6%. The structural feedback loop (higher rates → higher debt service → wider deficit → more bond supply → higher rates) has no visible exit valve. $250B bipartisan defense spending adds fiscal pressure. TBT is a 2x inverse of the 20+ Year Treasury — if yields grind higher through Q4 and into Q1 2027, TBT appreciates. Already up 14.4% since June. Exit condition: close if Fed signals a credible pause AND 10Y falls below 4.75%, which would signal the thesis has reversed.

AMD is the highest-quality expression of the CPU+GPU inference bifurcation thesis. Meta signed AMD as lead customer for MI450 accelerators AND Venice CPUs, issuing warrants for up to 160M shares — a structural demand commitment. AMD is up 23.6% since June but still has a clear catalyst path: Venice CPU roadmap for inference workloads, MI450 GPU ramp for training. Unlike Akamai (up 22% in one session on one deal with significant execution risk), AMD has diversified revenue across data center GPU, gaming, and now CPU inference — it's the broadest beneficiary if the workload splits from GPU-only training to GPU training + CPU inference. Exit condition: sell if Nvidia announces inference-optimized silicon that credibly recaptures CPU inference workloads, or if Meta cancels/reduces the Venice CPU commitment, or if AMD misses guidance by >10%.

Arista Networks is the highest-quality expression of AI infrastructure networking — every GPU training cluster, inference farm, and data center requires high-speed Ethernet switching, and Arista dominates with 40%+ market share. $9.6B in supply commitments signals visibility. Unlike chip plays, networking infrastructure is non-fungible (customers don't rip-and-replace switches easily), creating durable recurring revenue. Up 40% YTD but RS line at new highs suggests trend intact. Just added to S&P 100, which creates index-related buying demand. Sizing $20K as a satellite diversifier within the AI infrastructure theme (AMD is my primary expression). Exit condition: sell if AI capex broadly decelerates (two consecutive quarters of hyperscaler capex cuts), or if ANET loses major customer relationships to Cisco/Juniper alternatives.

Pre-earnings concentration reduction. META is ~60% of portfolio with Q3 earnings on October 28 — a binary event 29 days out. Thesis remains fully intact (Muse AI agent monetization, 3.4M downloads, zero sell ratings, Cantor $860 PT). This is purely portfolio risk management: selling 40 shares (385→345) to bring concentration from ~60% to ~54% before the October 28 catalyst. The Oct 28 print will be the first hard data on Muse paid conversion rates, and the market is priced for a strong showing. If results disappoint, a 60% concentration would cause catastrophic portfolio damage. Selling into strength (still +271% on cost basis from $198.53 avg). Will not trim further before earnings unless a specific bearish catalyst emerges.

Adding to macro rate hedge ahead of binary macro events this week: PCE Wednesday (expected +0.3% core, still well above 2% target) and September jobs Friday. Fed rate hike odds at 70-72.5% for October 28. Fed Governor Barr: 'no clear trend toward timely return to 2%.' Fed Governor Cook: AI buildout adding inflationary pressure. NY Fed Williams: another hike 'reasonable.' Bank of America projecting two more hikes (Oct + Dec). J.P. Morgan sees hikes going 'out with a bang.' The structural rate feedback loop (higher rates → higher deficit → more bond supply → higher rates) has no near-term exit. PCE printing Wednesday is almost certain to confirm inflation above target, cementing October hike odds. Adding $15K to bring TBT total to ~$65K (~13.7% of equity), squarely in the 10-15% macro hedge target band. TBT is 2x inverse 20+ year Treasury — direct beneficiary of sustained elevated/rising long yields.

Clean-sheet rebuild. AAPL carries no thesis. Two shares bought by the account owner before Andiamo existed — never a signal, never a conviction. At $330/share, Apple is a premium consumer hardware brand with no meaningful AI differentiation, decelerating Services growth, and no tailwind from the current macro regime. No position survives a zero-conviction filter.

Clean-sheet rebuild. Massive concentration reduction: from 53% to 20% of portfolio. META thesis is genuine — Muse now at 5M downloads, subscription monetization underway, dominant AI agent platform — but a 53% single-name bet on a binary Oct 28 earnings event is portfolio construction malpractice, not a strategy. From scratch, this is a 20% position: strong conviction, well-sized, with cash available to add if the Oct 28 print validates Muse paid conversion. The Oct 28 earnings need to prove Muse is a revenue engine, not just a download chart. Holding 129 shares (~$94K, 20%). Exit condition: sell entirely if Muse paid conversion disappoints on Oct 28, or if CapEx guidance implies 'costs not investment' framing.

Clean-sheet rebuild — resizing TBT from 13.9% to 10% of portfolio. The structural thesis holds: 10Y at 5.23%, fiscal deficit expands supply permanently, December hike at 100% certainty. But October hike has collapsed from 70% to 38% after Goldman's shift and PCE miss, making this an instrument with near-term headwinds: NFP Friday is binary, and a <80K print kills October odds entirely with possible short-term TLT rally. The thesis is structurally intact but the sizing should reflect current uncertainty. Reducing from 1,551 to ~1,099 shares keeps meaningful exposure while trimming the oversized position that was built on a higher-conviction October timing assumption.

Clean-sheet portfolio sizing discipline. AMD Venice thesis is real (5th consecutive record quarter, 2027 supply exhausted), but the valuation is not: 40x forward earnings vs NVDA at 25x, with the hyperscaler Arm chip shift (Graviton/Cobalt/Axion) taking x86 sockets from AMD's TAM. NVDA holds the structural advantage on the Arm transition because Arm proliferation validates its ecosystem while pressuring AMD's x86 franchise. Small trim of 4 shares brings AMD to clean 7% portfolio weight. The Venice thesis earns a position; the valuation premium vs NVDA does not earn a bigger one.

New position — AI GPU structural monopoly at a better price than AMD. NVDA data center revenue +117% YoY ($89B trailing 12M). Vera CPU now in production and expands TAM directly into AMD EPYC territory — uniquely positioned to capture both GPU and CPU AI spending. Trades at 25x forward P/E vs AMD at 40x, despite being the superior AI infrastructure franchise. The NVLink/CUDA moat is unmatched. Meanwhile AMD's Arm-transition headwinds (hyperscalers building custom Arm chips that take x86 sockets) strengthen NVDA's ecosystem since Arm proliferation validates NVDA's architecture strategy. The 'why not NVDA at 25x when AMD trades at 40x' question now has a clean answer: NVDA is more compelling from scratch. Target: 15% of portfolio. Exit: if AMD materially closes the AI GPU gap or if hyperscaler capex guidance cuts sharply.

Adding to ANET to reach 8% target weight (from current 4.2%). Arista is the AI networking backbone: $9.6B in supply commitments, 40% revenue growth guidance, EOS and CloudVision platforms creating genuine switching costs. Every AI data center needs high-speed ethernet switching — ANET is one of the only pure-plays on AI infrastructure spending that isn't directly competing with NVDA. At $199-215 range, fresh attention from analyst coverage and fund letters citing it as still undervalued despite 40% YTD. The Madison fund sell is a yellow flag but does not break the thesis — could be rotation/rebalance, not a fundamental view. Exit condition: revenue growth decelerates below 25%, or if Meta/hyperscalers shift architectures away from Ethernet.

New position — AI security cycle thesis. CrowdStrike +26% revenue growth, platform consolidation accelerating as enterprise IT complexity rises. The agentic AI proliferation is creating a massive new attack surface: every Muse/Dots agent, every MCP endpoint, every automated API call is a new entry point that requires CRWD's Falcon platform. Security spend historically is the last budget cut and often grows counter-cyclically. At ~$265, CRWD is a high-conviction idea in a macro environment where: (1) AI agent adoption is hockey-sticking; (2) cybersecurity spend follows AI spend with a lag; (3) platform consolidation favors CRWD's all-in-one approach. 8% position — satellite conviction, not core. Exit: revenue growth <15%, or if a major platform breach collapses enterprise trust.

New position — defensive ballast. Healthcare sector ETF (XLV) provides non-cyclical, rate-resilient earnings exposure in a portfolio otherwise concentrated in high-multiple AI infrastructure. With NFP Friday (Oct 2) as a live recession-fear binary, and consumer confidence at 12.5-year lows, the portfolio needs an asymmetric defensive position: XLV outperforms in a weak-jobs/recession-fear scenario, holds in a soft-landing scenario, and only underperforms if the Fed pivots to aggressive cuts (which is NOT the current trajectory with December hike at 100%). Healthcare earnings are structurally non-cyclical: people don't stop needing drugs, devices, and hospital visits when rates rise. 8% position. Exit: if the Fed signals an end to the hiking cycle and growth/risk-on dominates defensives.
